title: The Display Unit's screen and its bridge
ask: Which display does the Display Unit get, now that no store sells the 900 to 1000 nit bar and no ready-made HDMI bridge exists?
why: You ruled a 900 to 1000 nit bar display through an HDMI bridge (D-269). Looking for it to buy tonight, no store had that display: Waveshare's 12.3inch HDMI LCD is 600 nit, its 12.3inch 1920x720 LCD is 300 nit, and the brightest found, the HannStar HSD123KPW2-D10 panel sold in VSDISPLAY kits, is listed at 850 nit. And no ready-made bridge board was found: the BT817 board gives parallel RGB on a 50-pin flat cable (or LVDS on a 40-pin one, up to 1280 x 800), and nothing sold takes that and gives HDMI - the TFP410 is a chip, so the bridge is a small board to draw and order. The answer decides what the DU's screen is and when the display chain can be lit on the bench. Everything else for the DU and the CU is in tonight's carts.
options:
(a) The 850 nit HannStar panel with an HDMI driver board, and I draw the bridge board (TFP410, the BT817 board's 50-pin cable in, HDMI out) to order with the next boards. About 110 to 250 USD for the panel kit by the listings seen, the bridge a few dollars of board and parts. 50 to 150 nit under your ruling. Nothing arrives tonight; the display chain is lit when the bridge board is back.
(b) The 600 nit Waveshare 12.3inch HDMI LCD, 169.99 USD, in the box with its driver board, cables and a 12 V supply, and I draw the same bridge board. It can be ordered tonight. It is the brightness you ruled out for sun on the dash.
(c) Keep 900 to 1000 nit and I keep looking (industrial and automotive panel sellers, by quote). Nothing is bought for the display now; the DU is built and run without its screen until one is found.
(d) Drop the HDMI bridge and scaler: a panel the BT817 board drives directly on its LVDS connector, at most 1280 x 800. No bridge to draw, but not the 1920 x 720 bar you ruled, and the pages are redrawn to it.
recommend: (a), unless 850 nit is not bright enough for you - then (c)
stops: ordering P118 and P119, ticking Y16, and F3's display bring-up (the DU's boards, radio and firmware go ahead without it)

title: Rows that could come after the carts
ask: Should the vehicle carts wait for Ionic's reply and for the firmware rows, or may the design be frozen without them?
why:
You asked for every step before the shopping and the strip to be looked at, and moved after wherever it can go. Most were clear and are done: the strip now waits only on the two units and on the checks that need the car whole, and the cluster render and the alternator look no longer hold the review. Two groups are left. Both hold the design review, and so the freeze and the vehicle carts, although nothing in a cart turns on either.

1. The Ionic e-mail (W-330b) and my row that reads its reply (V-052): the Bluetooth map for current and state of charge, the battery heater's figures, what the battery does below freezing, its charge limit. Waiting costs: the carts wait on someone else's reply, or on you saying in the app that none came. Moving risks: if the reply shows the battery cannot report its current, a current shunt at the battery - one part and one wire in the cargo bin - is added after the carts as a second small order. The surge clamp for a battery cut-out is already in the design.

2. The firmware rows - B7 logging, B8 two boards on one bus, F-007 the odometer surviving a power cut, F-010 settings on the memory card, F-014 where each signal comes from, F14 the display's bus traffic - and T-049, the memory card they wait on. Waiting costs you only T-049, five minutes with a card; but these rows have stuck before on tools I could not run, and the carts would wait with them. Moving risks: the review reads the design with the firmware unfinished; a firmware fault found late is a re-flash over USB, or at worst a change to a board, which the board order already risks. The odometer row would still hold the meters cutover.
options:
(a) Neither group holds the carts. Both come out of the review's list; the firmware rows hold instead the day the two units are plugged into the car, and the Ionic rows hold nothing in the build. Costs nothing now. The risks are the two above: a shunt possibly added later, and firmware reviewed after the freeze.
(b) Only the Ionic rows come out; the firmware rows still finish before the review. The carts can no longer wait on Ionic, but can still wait on a stuck firmware row.
(c) Only the firmware rows come out; the carts wait for Ionic's reply, or for your word that none came.
(d) Leave both where they are: the review and the carts wait for all of it. Costs nothing but the wait.
recommend: (a), unless you want the review to read finished firmware - then (b)
stops: Nothing today. It decides what the design review (Z1), and so the freeze and the vehicle carts, wait on.

title: The connectors to buy so every leg plugs in
ask: May I add the start relay socket's terminals and seals to the parts list now, and add each other mating connector as its part is chosen or its plug is seen?
why:
You ruled that every leg ends in the plug its part needs. Each of the 59 parts the harness reaches now has its plug written down, how that is known, and how its end is made: 27 keep their factory plug (cut off the old harness and joined on, as you ruled), 11 end in our own Deutsch plugs, 9 take a ring or spade on a stud or tab, 2 have no harness end, and 10 are new parts that need a connector of their own. Nobody has seen any of these plugs yet: for the factory parts the 1982 diagram gives only how many wires each has, never the maker or a part number, and your looks during the strip settle the rest.

Of the 10 new ones, one is a sure purchase that is on no list today: the sealed socket for the start relay beside the starter (P005, already on the Waytek cart) is sold without its five terminals and five seals, by Waytek's listing as a search returned it - the page itself would not load, so I read it properly before anything is ordered. The servos' leads are already on the list. The rest cannot be named yet: four wait on the part being chosen (the ignition switch, the brake pedal switch, the road-speed sensor, the USB socket) and one on the amplifier; three come with their part if the box is complete (the head unit's power cord, the wideband gauge's lead, the LED headlamps' adapter) and are checked when the box is opened.
options:
(a) Add the start relay socket's terminals and seals to the parts list now, on the Waytek cart beside the socket - a few dollars. Each other connector is added to its own part's line when that part is chosen or its plug has been seen, without a new question unless one costs more than about 20 USD. Closes off nothing.
(b) Add nothing now. I bring you one complete list of connectors after your looks during the strip, before the carts are paid. Costs nothing now; it adds one more question later, and the relay socket's terminals wait with the rest.
(c) Buy a new connector for every factory part as well, so the old harness is left whole - the second set of plugs you turned down when you chose to cut the plugs off. About 27 plugs whose maker no document gives: each has to be identified from your photos first. The most money and the most time.
recommend: (a), unless you would rather see one complete list after the strip - then (b)
stops: Nothing today. The vehicle carts should not be paid until the plug looks from the strip are filed, so no part is found at the install to need a plug nobody bought.
